code.framework_path: PostgreSQL -> Daft -> Arrow -> Ray task -> vLLM

scale_probe.purpose: diagnose whether increasing row count alone creates adaptive batches
scale_probe.interpretation: screening only; policy order was not randomized
scale_probe.decision: do not spend a 2048-row run before fixing window selection and event-time catch-up

incident.symptom: seven vLLM requests remained running after a 180-second client timeout
incident.recovery: restart only the experimental vLLM container, wait for health=200 and running=waiting=0, then rerun the complete policy group
incident.limitation: policy order was not randomized and the service restart occurred only before the successful queue_adaptive group

claim_boundary: This is an accelerated controlled arrival workload, not a literal production-rate replay.
Submission latency is batch-level; per-request end-to-end latency was not captured.
The experiment screens flush policies on one GPU and does not establish multi-GPU behavior.
Overlapping confidence intervals and non-randomized policy order preclude a significance claim.
